findings.counterexample: Any oracle-fail or policy-fail slot entering selected quality records would contaminate the Gate.
findings.pass_condition: Exactly 9 selected records, balanced cases CASE-001 and CASE-002, depth 1 and no terminal-negative quality selection.
findings.statement: Independent projection yields 9 quality-eligible slots, two balanced cases and minimum repeat depth one; 14 terminal-negative slots remain quality-ineligible.

findings.counterexample: Deleting a failed, infrastructure-censored or retry attempt biases reliability.
findings.pass_condition: The exact counts and rounded rates reproduce from all 28 frozen attempts.
findings.statement: All 28 attempts remain in reliability: 20 completed, 18 primary-eligible, 16 terminal, 7 policy, 1 infrastructure and 4 retries.

findings.counterexample: Counting CASE-001-ARM-A-R2 as success or terminal negative overstates completeness.
findings.pass_condition: Resolution counts are 9, 14 and 1 censored, with three fully resolved cases at depth two.
findings.statement: The matrix resolves 23 of 24 slots: 9 successes and 14 terminal negatives; CASE-001-ARM-A-R2 remains harness-censored.

findings.counterexample: Using the mixed infrastructure attempt as a gap solely from secondary flags would violate scope separation.
findings.pass_condition: Only repeated oracle and policy terminal groups are eligible; censored and recovery evidence remain excluded.
findings.statement: Repeated component-gap groups contain 9 oracle failures and 7 policy failures; infrastructure and harness censoring are excluded.

findings.counterexample: Substituting schedule or outcome depth two for quality depth one would reverse the quality Gate.
findings.pass_condition: All six named metrics reproduce independently and success_after_retry remains empty.
findings.statement: The six scoped repeat values are 2, 1, 3, 2, 2 and 2; unscoped repeat_depth is deprecated and no retry fills quality evidence.
